description: Gradle 9.7.0 exposes its own lib/javaparser-core-3.27.1.jar on the system classloader (9.6.1 exposed it only on the Gradle API classloader).
kapt's annotation-processor classloader delegates parent-first, so Micronaut's Java processors link against that 3.27.1 instead of the 3.28.0 on the kapt classpath and :server:kaptKotlin fails with
NoSuchMethodError: StaticJavaParser.parseJavadoc(String, boolean) (javaparser 3.28.0 replaced the 1-arg overload that 3.27.1 provides).
Remove this rule once a Gradle release no longer leaks javaparser onto the system classloader — verify by flipping distributionUrl and running ./gradlew test.
Track the Debian release the Docker base image is built on.

gradle/libs.versions.toml pins it as `debian`, and .github/docker/Dockerfile interpolates it into the image *name* — gcr.io/distroless/java-base-debian13 — so the release is not a tag Renovate could follow on that image. It is followed on the debian image instead.

distroless publishes one variant per Debian release, so a bump is only valid once java-base-debian<release> exists; nothing on a pull request builds the image, so that has to be checked by hand before merging.
The versioning admits whole releases only: debian also tags point releases (13.6) and codenames (trixie), and neither names a distroless variant.
